text: DEMO REPAIR PROCEDURE — NOT MANUFACTURER DOCUMENTATION. Touring Model Rear Axle Installation. During rear wheel installation, inspect the axle, spacers, wheel bearings, and axle threads for damage before assembly. Install the rear axle and tighten the rear axle nut to 95 ft-lb (129 Nm). After tightening, verify correct wheel alignment, free wheel rotation, and proper brake operation before returning the vehicle to service.

DEMO SERVICE BULLETIN — NOT MANUFACTURER DOCUMENTATION. Bulletin TCU-0142 addresses intermittent false diagnostic fault codes reported by the telematics control unit. Affected vehicles may display communication-related fault codes even when the telematics hardware is operating normally. Technicians should verify battery voltage, inspect TCU connectors, record the diagnostic codes, and confirm the currently installed software version. If the vehicle meets the bulletin criteria, update the telematics control unit to the approved software release and clear the stored false fault codes. Hardware replacement should not be performed solely because of the false codes described in this bulletin.

DEMO WARRANTY POLICY — NOT MANUFACTURER DOCUMENTATION. Certified Pre-Owned Powertrain Coverage. An eligible transmission replacement is covered for 24 months or 24,000 miles from the certified pre-owned vehicle delivery date, whichever occurs first. Coverage requires confirmation that the vehicle remains within the applicable CPO coverage period and that the failure meets covered-component requirements. Normal wear, unauthorized modifications, and damage caused by misuse are excluded from this demonstration policy.

DEMO WARRANTY POLICY — NOT MANUFACTURER DOCUMENTATION. Brake System Claim Approval Workflow. Brake system repair claims require technician diagnosis and supporting repair documentation before final approval. A claim must not be automatically pre-approved solely from the initial dealer submission when technician review is required. The technician findings, diagnostic evidence, affected components, and proposed repair must be recorded before the warranty reviewer makes the final coverage decision.
